scope: Text-only semantic audit of the four exact saved Mini/Qwen replies against their complete frozen raw provider inputs, incorporating the narrow HR-005-v1 adjudication.
reviewer_capability: No raster image inspection in this audit. Findings compare reply claims to frozen OCR/context and do not certify printed wording or scan-grounded readings.

human_overlay.decision: Stephen confirms the AI's Mr. Wade attribution for this specific reply and following paragraph.
human_overlay.scope_limit: Output-informed case-specific adjudication only; no blanket contextual OCR-name repair rule, authority/person ID, or general accuracy claim. No re-ask.

omissions: P1 ('The amendment was agreed to') receives no attribution, consistent with a procedural result rather than a named speaking turn.
uncertainty_or_role_confusion: P3-P5 are proposed statutory sections introduced by Wade. The output assigns them to Wade's floor-speaker turn; this may mean he presents/reads the amendment, but the role vocabulary does not distinguish speaker from the embedded legislative text. Treat as scope ambiguity, not a demonstrated factual error.

One output block uses candidate C1 while citing cue C3 for P7-P13 and P15-P16. Both C1 and C3 contain the raw name Mr. WADE, but cue aliases are not person authority IDs; the output does not express a durable identity resolution. HR-005 supports only P15-P16.

reply_reviews.source: part 1, leaf 487, printed page 371; one supplied target paragraph
source_backed_correct: The single supplied paragraph is first-person political speech, but it contains no explicit speaker-name cue; leaving the floor speaker unknown is supported by this limited input.
Davis and President appear as mentions/examples in the argument, not as floor speakers.
omissions: The OCR-derived cue fragment C3 ('uard') is not assigned; abstention is appropriate because it does not establish a named speaker.
uncertainty_or_role_confusion: The two person_mentioned rows say the mentions are not speaking turns, but encode status proposed with candidate_id null. This is semantically cautious yet internally inconsistent under both contracts; the whole reply remains invalid and is not partially salvaged.

No authority identity is supported for the generic title 'President'; the model appropriately avoids naming an officeholder, but its null-candidate proposed row cannot be serialized as a valid assignment.

reply_reviews.source: part 1, leaf 487, printed page 371; same supplied target paragraph and cues
source_backed_correct: Unknown floor-speaker attribution cites P1 as evidence: the paragraph shows a speaking turn while providing no supported identity. This is the intended v2 behavior.
Davis and President are classified as mentioned people rather than the floor speaker, matching the raw paragraph.
omissions: The damaged cue fragment C3 ('uard') is not promoted to a person or speaker, appropriately preserving uncertainty.
uncertainty_or_role_confusion: The President mention is generic in this passage; C2 remains a source cue alias, not a resolved individual or authority. The output does not supply a historical identity, which is appropriate.

P1 is an entire long paragraph containing mixed arguments and mentions. The unknown floor-speaker target is paragraph-scoped because no smaller evidence spans are available; this is not a claim that every subspan has identical role scope.
reply_reviews.structural_status: Invalid in v1 solely because unknown carried paragraph evidence; valid under v2. No semantic rows were edited or salvaged.

coverage_gaps: Only two of six frozen windows have saved model outputs, both on parts 1 and 5. The other frozen windows, parts 2-4, and broader chapter/context diversity remain untested by these four replies.

No date-positive prediction was tested. Frozen 'may' cues are lexical false positives by source-review expectation, but these four role replies do not test date outputs; there is no date-positive/date-negative model result here.
Boundary behavior is tested only in the Wade continuation/interruption sample. No explicit boundary-stop case tests that a prior speaker/date/proceeding must not carry into a subsequent proceeding.
No scan images were inspected in this audit; OCR-grounded name/number correctness and print fidelity remain unassessed except for the narrow human HR-005 adjudication.

smallest_next_preparation.decision: Keep protocol v2 unchanged for now; prepare a two-window offline date/stop diagnostic before considering any further model call.

window_1_reuse.use: Reuse the frozen raw input unchanged as a date-negative plus boundary-stop case. Its 'may' cue is a lexical false positive; use explicit local turns (Kasson, Holmes, subsequent proceedings) to test stopping attribution at named turns and proceeding transitions. 'Mr. Speaker' remains a title, not a named identity.
window_1_reuse.source_review: Existing frozen expectation says keep Kasson/Holmes/later turns local; mixed paragraphs need review.

window_2_select.use: Select one short source window with an explicit printed full date in the text, plus the adjacent turn/proceeding needed to test date scope. Freeze exact raw context, date kind/precision, source anchors, and an expected non-propagation boundary before any output.
window_2_select.guardrail: Do not infer a date from catalog metadata or select a source/date value until the exact source passage and provenance are frozen.

smallest_next_preparation.next_decision: After offline selection/source review, decide whether the date task should be a separate contract from speaker-role output. Do not spend calls on the four untouched cases until date-positive evidence and a concrete boundary-stop input are frozen; no human grade or launch approval is implied by this audit.

conclusion: The saved replies show structurally valid, text-supported role distinctions on the cross-page diagnostic, with HR-005 narrowly resolving P15-P16. The unnamed case shows v2 fixes Qwen's paragraph-evidence abstention; Mini remains invalid due to proposed rows without candidates. The sample supports the serialization change only and does not establish broad semantic accuracy, date behavior, or boundary-stop reliability.
